outcome_summary: 9 of 19 eligible rows already carried a Donaldson-verified base from the prior pass. This exception-closure pass adds 5 more Donaldson-verified bases (P550390 for the two standard/high-capacity N-Series and F-Series fuel pairs, and P550420 for the F-Series 1987-2008 lube row), resolved by applying an OEM-vs-CROSSREF Donaldson evidence-tier distinction the prior pass had not used, and cross-verified every reused SKU against data/dims.csv physical dimensions. One row (P2-N-TRANS) moves from CONFLICTING to BLOCKED_DONALDSON after its only Donaldson hit was rejected as a false-positive category mismatch (a transmission filter cartridge cannot be a full-flow engine-oil spin-on). One row (P2-N-LUBE-1998-2010) remains genuinely CONFLICTING: the disputed Isuzu number ties to two different Donaldson parts at the identical CROSSREF evidence tier, with no defensible tie-breaker found despite exhaustive first-party-capture research. Zero Fleetguard bases exist anywhere in this file -- no row has ever reached DONALDSON_NOT_MANUFACTURED_VERIFIED. A duplicate-canonical-mapping audit across every Donaldson part touched by Isuzu Phase 3 found one legacy-CSV stale mapping (P550008, three orphaned MANN-sourced SKUs never reconciled to dims.csv) that is not actionable here because P550008 is not used as a base for any Isuzu row. SINGLE-CASE MICROINVESTIGATION 2026-09-24 then resolved the file's one remaining CONFLICTING row (P2-N-LUBE-1998-2010) using Donaldson equipment-application records: P502042 (ELIMFILTERS EL82042, reused) explicitly serves the 4HE1-TC/4HK1-TC engines this row is scoped to, while the competing candidate P550973 explicitly serves only an unrelated older Isuzu engine family and is rejected. CONFLICTING is now 0 across the entire file. BLOCKED_DONALDSON CLOSURE MICRO-PHASE 2026-09-24 then resolved 2 of the file's 4 remaining BLOCKED_DONALDSON rows: P2-N-LUBE-2011-ON and P2-F-LUBE-2018-2021 (shared Isuzu OE 8982984040) both identify Donaldson P848076 via official product title plus distributor corroboration, now NO_ELIMFILTERS_SKU_YET pending SKU governance. The other 2 (P2-N-FWS-2022i-ON, P2-N-TRANS) stay BLOCKED_DONALDSON with precise, non-generic root causes after exhaustive re-investigation (a rejected false-positive Donaldson candidate, and confirmation the transmission is Aisin RNJ, not Allison). BLOCKED_DONALDSON is now 2 across the entire file.

caveats: SINGLE-CASE MICROINVESTIGATION 2026-09-24: the tie between P502042 and P550973 for the disputed number 2906548000 is resolved not by evidence tier (both are CROSSREF-tier for this exact number, as the prior pass found) and not by family-level OEM-tie count (which favoured P550973 and was explicitly NOT used as proof), but by direct EQUIPMENT-APPLICATION evidence from scripts/donaldson_lube_results.json: P502042's own equipment list names 4HE1-TC and 4HK1-TC engines in NPR/NQR/NPS trucks -- the exact two engines Phase 1 assigns to every block this row binds to (N-2000-2001, N-2002-2004: 4HE1-TC; N-2005-2010: 4HK1-TC). P550973's equipment list names only the 4BB1/4BD1/4BD2 engine family, which Phase 1 never assigns to any Isuzu diesel block in this closure. This is an objective platform mismatch, not a preference.

Donaldson's own 'Primary Application' field further distinguishes the two products: P502042's is ISUZU 8970967770, P550973's is ISUZU 8970492820 -- two different designated primary Isuzu references, neither of which is the disputed 2906548000 itself. Both parts' 'alternatives' arrays are empty in Donaldson's data, so Donaldson itself does not declare a supersession or alternate relationship between them: they are two distinct, unrelated products that happen to share a thread size (1 1/2-12 UN) and both absorbed the same third-party-aggregated Isuzu CROSSREF entry for 2906548000.

Physical comparison confirms two different products, not a data duplicate: P502042 is 124mm x 120mm with a bypass valve and 16-micron/50% efficiency media (JIS D 1611); P550973 is 123mm x 149mm (29mm longer) with no bypass valve and a coarser 50-micron/99% media. Both are dims.csv-verified, currently-catalogued, distinct ELIMFILTERS SKUs (EL82042, EL80973) -- selecting P502042 does not create or resolve a duplicate mapping, it simply declines to use P550973 for this specific Isuzu row.

2906542701 and 2906548100, the other two numbers in this Phase 2 row, remain unconfirmed by Donaldson anywhere in the first-party capture (checked again this pass: flat CSV, lube/fuel/air results, competitor matrix, OEM matrix, import-ready, homologation matrix -- zero hits). Only 2906548000 is Donaldson-recognised, and only via the CROSSREF tier on P502042 (and, rejected, on P550973). This is why the decision is PARTIAL rather than a full closure of the row, independent of the Phase 2 row's own PARTIAL evidence_status which caps decision_status at PARTIAL regardless.
